description:
FILED s543u (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28) while probing #5560 (`s/a\Kb/<$1>/` with no group).

THE SHAPE (perl 5.40.3 vs 5d511ff8):
    (my $x = "ab") =~ s/ab/<$1>/; print "$x\n";      # perl <>     PCL: Lisp error, backtrace, exit 1
    (my $y = "ab") =~ s/(a)(b)/[$3$2]/g; print "$y\n"; # perl [b]   PCL: the same error

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp perl-to-ppcre-replacement turned every $N of a constant replacement into cl-ppcre's template \N, and cl-ppcre's build-replacement refuses a register the pattern does not have.

=== DONE (s543u) ===
perl-to-ppcre-replacement takes the pattern's group count (the closers vector %pcl-create-scanner returns: one entry per capturing group the program wrote) and writes nothing for a $N past it -- perl's undef, the empty string.  N is every digit after the `$`, as perl reads `$12`.  Guard: Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t row 72 (FAILS on the 5d511ff8 extraction).
frequency_reason: a replacement naming a group the pattern lacks is a program slip; found by s543u probing \K without a group, no program known to hold it
subject: CRASH: a template replacement naming a group past the pattern's (`s/ab/<$1>/`) was a Lisp error from cl-ppcre ("Reference to non-existent register 1 in replacement string", a backtrace); perl's $1 is undef there, the empty string -- FIXED in s543u
triage_reason: core s/// semantics (perlop); a Lisp backtrace is never a perl answer
